newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson rejects Goldman confession offer.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson rejects Goldman confession offer.

text.p: O.J. Simpson refused on Wednesday to confess to the murders of his ex-wife and her friend, saying he would never admit he was guilty of a crime he did not commit.

He was responding to an offer made by victim Ronald Goldman's father Fred, who said he would give up all claims to the $21 million he won against Simpson if the former football star would confess to the murders of his son and Nicole Brown Simpson.

A jury last week blamed Simpson for the June 12, 1994, killings of his ex-wife and Goldman, who were stabbed and slashed to death outside Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium. Simpson was acquitted of the murders by a criminal court jury in October, 1995.

"If the person, whose name I don't use, that murdered my son wants to write out a complete confession and publish it in newspapers around the country, we'll be glad to ignore the judgment," Goldman said in a radio interview on Wednesday.
In a statement issued through one of his lawyers, Phil Baker, Simpson said: "No matter how much money I am offered, I would never confess to a crime which I did not commit."

Daniel Petrocelli, who represented Fred Goldman during Simpson's wrongful death civil trial, expanded on his client's offer on Wednesday night on CNN's "Larry King Live" show saying, "He has to confess that he killed Ronald Goldman and Nicole Brown Simspon, he has to tell the world what he did and how he did it and sign his name to a confession."
In finding Simpson "liable" for the deaths of Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman, the jury awarded compensatory damages of $8.5 million to be shared by Goldman's divorced parents.
After a second round of deliberations, jurors on Monday added $12.5 million in punitive damages for Goldman's relatives and an equal sum for the estate of Nicole Brown Simpson.

Fred Goldman, who pursued the civil case against Simpson, said in an interview with the Salem Radio Network, a national broadcaster, that he did not care about the money but about assigning blame for his son's murder.

However, he said he did not expect Simpson to agree to his terms. "That'll never happen, never going to happen," Goldman said. "This person hasn't (taken) full responsibility for any of his actions in his lifetime."
Simpson has steadfastly maintained his innocence throughout both his criminal and civil trials.
